venues.name: Aman New York
venues.note: A hushed vertical sanctuary in the Crown Building, the city, finally, on silent.

venues.name: The Mark Hotel
venues.note: The Upper East Side's most glamorous house, the only New York hotel on the world list.
credentials: World's 50 Best Hotels 2025 (No. 43, only NYC entry)

venues.name: The Carlyle, A Rosewood Hotel
venues.note: Old-New-York grandeur with a cabaret in the basement, the city's most storied address.

venues.name: The Peninsula New York
venues.note: A Beaux-Arts landmark on Fifth, with the group's famous precision and a rooftop bar.

venues.name: Mandarin Oriental, New York
venues.note: Park-and-skyline views from on high at Columbus Circle, the group's calm, precise flagship.

venues.name: Four Seasons Hotel New York Downtown
venues.note: The surest hands in Lower Manhattan, service you never have to think about.

venues.name: The St. Regis New York
venues.note: The house that invented the butler, Astor-era Beaux-Arts splendour off Fifth Avenue.

venues.name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, Central Park
venues.note: Park-facing tradition on Central Park South, grand, gracious, and reliably excellent.

venues.name: Baccarat Hotel New York
venues.note: Crystal-chandelier glamour opposite MoMA, a jewel-box of a hotel, and it knows it.

venues.name: Park Hyatt New York
venues.note: A calm, contemporary tower on Billionaires' Row, quiet luxury, beautifully run.

venues.name: The Towers at Lotte New York Palace
venues.note: A hotel-within-a-hotel in a Gilded-Age courtyard mansion, the exclusive Towers wing.

venues.name: Casa Cipriani New York
venues.note: A members'-club hotel in a landmark ferry terminal, Italian glamour on the water's edge.

venues.name: Crosby Street Hotel, Firmdale Hotels
venues.note: Firmdale's English-country-house colour dropped into the heart of SoHo.

venues.name: The Whitby Hotel, Firmdale Hotels
venues.note: A joyful, art-filled Firmdale house a whisper from Fifth Avenue and Central Park.

venues.name: The Lowell
venues.note: A discreet townhouse hotel of wood fires and fresh flowers, old-money calm.

venues.name: The Greenwich Hotel
venues.note: Robert De Niro's Tribeca hideaway, a warm, worldly house with a lantern-lit pool.

venues.name: The Fifth Avenue Hotel
venues.note: A gilded mansion-and-tower debut, maximalist, romantic, the talk of NoMad.

venues.name: Hotel Barrière Fouquet's New York
venues.note: Parisian glamour on the Hudson side of Tribeca, the Champs-Élysées, restaged downtown.

venues.name: Pendry Manhattan West
venues.note: A sleek new-build in the Hudson Yards district, polished, contemporary, well-run.

venues.name: Warren Street Hotel, Firmdale Hotels
venues.note: Firmdale's downtown debut, the same fearless colour, now in Tribeca.

venues.name: Nine Orchard
venues.note: A landmark 1912 bank turned design-led hotel, the coolest room downtown.

venues.name: 1 Hotel Central Park
venues.note: Nature-led calm steps from Central Park, reclaimed wood, living walls, easy comfort.

venues.name: The Beekman, A Thompson Hotel
venues.note: A breathtaking nine-storey Victorian atrium downtown, history with a modern pulse.

venues.name: The Wall Street Hotel
venues.note: A quietly elegant house in the old financial heart, a calm downtown residence.

venues.name: The Mercer
venues.note: The original SoHo loft hotel, spare, timeless, and endlessly cool.

venues.name: The Bowery Hotel
venues.note: A dimly-lit, velvet-and-candles downtown classic, romantic and a little bohemian.

venues.name: The Ludlow Hotel
venues.note: A relaxed, downtown-cool house on the Lower East Side, effortless and unpretentious.

venues.name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, NoMad
venues.note: A tall, contemporary Ritz-Carlton with a rooftop over the Empire State Building.

venues.name: The Surrey, A Corinthia Hotel
venues.note: A refined Upper East Side residence, newly reborn under Corinthia, quiet, gracious calm.

venues.name: The Twenty Two New York
venues.note: The London members'-club hotel's first New York address, buzzy and of-the-moment.

venues.name: Hotel Chelsea
venues.note: The most legendary bohemian hotel in America, reborn, and steeped in its own myth.

venues.name: 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge
venues.note: The best Manhattan-skyline view in the city, from the Brooklyn side of the river.

venues.name: Wythe Hotel
venues.note: A converted Williamsburg factory with a rooftop bar and the skyline across the water.

venues.name: Ace Hotel Brooklyn
venues.note: A design-led, art-filled house in brownstone Brooklyn, relaxed and creative.

venues.name: The New York EDITION
venues.note: Understated elegance in a landmark clock tower over Madison Square Park.

venues.name: The Greenwich Hotel, Tribeca Penthouse
venues.note: A one-of-a-kind Japanese-crafted penthouse above the Greenwich, the city's most private suite.

venues.name: Trump International Hotel & Tower New York
venues.note: Full Central Park frontage at Columbus Circle, big windows, big views.

venues.name: Eleven Madison Park
venues.note: Daniel Humm's plant-based three-star, the most talked-about fine-dining room in America.

venues.name: Le Bernardin
venues.note: Eric Ripert's temple to seafood, three stars held for decades, and never a slip.

venues.name: Per Se
venues.note: Thomas Keller's New York flagship, a hushed room over Central Park, at the summit.

venues.name: Jungsik
venues.note: Yim Jungsik's modern Korean, the cuisine reimagined at the very highest level.

venues.name: Sushi Sho
venues.note: The city's newest three-star, a revered Tokyo master's edomae omakase.

venues.name: Atomix
venues.note: The Parks' Korean tasting counter, named the best restaurant in North America.

venues.name: Masa
venues.note: Masa Takayama's austere, extravagant sushi, still among the costliest meals in America.

venues.name: Daniel
venues.note: Daniel Boulud's grand French dining room, the Upper East Side's most elegant table.

venues.name: Jean-Georges
venues.note: Jean-Georges Vongerichten's flagship, light, precise French with a park view.

venues.name: The Modern
venues.note: Refined American cooking overlooking MoMA's sculpture garden, art on both sides of the glass.

venues.name: Gabriel Kreuther
venues.note: Alsatian-French cooking of real soul, overlooking Bryant Park.

venues.name: Aquavit
venues.note: The city's benchmark for Nordic cooking, cool, clean, and quietly luxurious.

venues.name: Aska
venues.note: Fredrik Berselius's Nordic tasting menu in a candlelit Williamsburg townhouse.

venues.name: Atera
venues.note: An intimate Tribeca counter of exacting, seasonal tasting menus.

venues.name: Saga
venues.note: A tasting menu high in a landmark 1930s skyscraper, the view is part of the meal.

venues.name: César
venues.note: A French-Japanese two-star that arrived fully formed, precise and personal.

venues.name: Chef's Table at Brooklyn Fare
venues.note: An intense, seafood-led counter, one of the city's most serious tasting experiences.

venues.name: Joo Ok
venues.note: A refined Korean tasting menu, newly elevated to two stars, quiet, considered, exact.

venues.name: Sushi Noz
venues.note: A hinoki-wood counter of pure edomae craft, sushi as meditation.

venues.name: Odo
venues.note: A serene kaiseki counter hidden behind a tea room, Japan, faithfully rendered.

venues.name: Semma
venues.note: The only Indian restaurant in America to hold a Michelin star, South India, uncompromised.

venues.name: Café Carmellini
venues.note: Andrew Carmellini's grand, romantic Italian-French room inside The Fifth Avenue Hotel.

venues.name: Torrisi
venues.note: Italian-American cooking with a New-York swagger, in the landmark Puck Building.

venues.name: Rezdôra
venues.note: A love letter to Emilia-Romagna, the city's most wanted pasta.

venues.name: Le Coucou
venues.note: A beautiful, candlelit ode to classical French cooking in the heart of SoHo.

venues.name: Crown Shy
venues.note: James Kent's downtown room, inventive, generous, and consistently excellent.

venues.name: The Dining Room at Gramercy Tavern
venues.note: A New York institution, seasonal American cooking of unwavering grace.

venues.name: COTE
venues.note: A Korean steakhouse of real refinement, the butcher's counter meets the tasting menu.

venues.name: Le Pavillon
venues.note: Daniel Boulud's soaring, garden-like room of vegetable- and seafood-led French cooking.

venues.name: Café Boulud at Maison Barnes
venues.note: Daniel Boulud's warm, seasonal café, refined French with an easy grace.

venues.name: Sushi Nakazawa
venues.note: A joyful, generous omakase from a Jiro-trained master, sushi with a smile.

venues.name: Corima
venues.note: Modern Northern Mexican cooking that earned a star within a year of opening.

venues.name: Dirt Candy
venues.note: Amanda Cohen's pioneering vegetable tasting menu, the case for vegetables, made joyfully.

venues.name: The Four Horsemen
venues.note: A wine bar that quietly became one of the country's best restaurants.

venues.name: Bridges
venues.note: A newly-starred Chinatown room bringing quiet French finesse to a downtown corner.

venues.name: Huso
venues.note: A caviar-and-seafood tasting counter of great luxury, newly starred.

venues.name: Yamada
venues.note: A precise new Japanese counter that earned its star straight out of the gate.

venues.name: Frevo
venues.note: An intimate tasting menu hidden behind an art-gallery door, French with a Brazilian pulse.

venues.name: Kono
venues.note: A tiny yakitori counter of great purity, every part of the bird over charcoal.

venues.name: Le Veau d'Or
venues.note: New York's oldest French bistro, lovingly revived, a piece of the city's soul.

venues.name: Via Carota
venues.note: The West Village trattoria everyone wants a table at, simple, perfect, always full.

venues.name: Dhamaka
venues.note: Unapologetic, rustic Indian cooking that pulls no punches, a love letter to the regions.

venues.name: Bungalow
venues.note: Vikas Khanna's ode to Indian country-club dining, glamorous, generous, joyful.

venues.name: Cardamom
venues.note: Modern Indian cooking with a light, contemporary hand, Bib-listed and easy to love.

venues.name: Chutney Masala
venues.note: Warm, well-made Indian cooking that quietly earned the inspectors' nod.

venues.name: HanGawi
venues.note: A serene, shoes-off Korean temple restaurant, entirely vegetarian, and quietly special.

venues.name: Coqodaq
venues.note: A glamorous Korean fried-chicken-and-Champagne room, serious fun, seriously good.

venues.name: Bonnie's
venues.note: Cantonese-American cooking with a Brooklyn wit, nostalgic and inventive at once.

venues.name: Atla
venues.note: Bright, all-day Mexican cooking from the Cosme team, fresh, light, and always buzzing.

venues.name: Oxomoco
venues.note: Wood-fired, one-star Mexican cooking in a sunlit Greenpoint room.

venues.name: Dim Sum Go Go
venues.note: A Chinatown stalwart doing precise, handmade dim sum, credentialed and beloved.

venues.name: CheLi
venues.note: Shanghainese home cooking done with real care, a Bib-listed crowd favourite.

venues.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
venues.note: Five thousand years of art in one building on Fifth Avenue, do the Temple of Dendur, the European paintings and the rooftop bar, then let the rest go; it's too big for one day.
credentials: One of the world's great encyclopedic museums
Most-visited museum in the United States

venues.name: The Museum of Modern Art (MoMA)
venues.note: Van Gogh's Starry Night, Monet's Water Lilies room, Warhol and Picasso, the modern canon in a light-filled building; go at opening or in the last two hours to dodge the crush.
credentials: One of the world's foremost modern-art museums

venues.name: The Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum
venues.note: Frank Lloyd Wright's white spiral is the reason to come as much as the art, take the lift up and walk the ramp down past the Kandinskys.

venues.name: The Frick Collection
venues.note: A steel baron's Fifth Avenue mansion hung with Vermeer, Rembrandt and Bellini, reopened April 2025 after a $220m restoration that finally opened the family's upstairs rooms to the public; the most civilised hour of art in the city.

venues.name: The Whitney Museum of American Art
venues.note: Renzo Piano's museum of American art at the foot of the High Line, Hopper, O'Keeffe, Basquiat inside, and terraces that frame the Hudson and downtown skyline for free.

venues.name: The Met Cloisters
venues.note: The Met's medieval outpost, built from real French monastery cloisters on a bluff over the Hudson, the Unicorn Tapestries, herb gardens and river views make the subway ride uptown worth it. A quiet gem most visitors miss.

venues.name: The Morgan Library & Museum
venues.note: J.P. Morgan's private study and jewel-box library, Gutenberg Bibles, illuminated manuscripts and a domed rotunda in the financier's own home. Small, sumptuous, rarely crowded.

venues.name: The American Museum of Natural History
venues.note: Blue whale, dinosaur halls and the Rose planetarium plus the new Gilder science wing, the single best half-day in the city for children and multi-generational groups.

venues.name: The Neue Galerie
venues.note: A small mansion museum for German and Austrian art, home to Klimt's gold Woman in Gold, with Café Sabarsky downstairs for Viennese pastry. A refined pairing of art and Kaffeehaus.

venues.name: The Noguchi Museum
venues.note: Isamu Noguchi's own studio turned into a museum of stone sculpture around a still garden, a meditative escape a short hop across the river. Pair it with nearby Socrates Sculpture Park.

venues.name: 9/11 Memorial & Museum
venues.note: Two black reflecting pools in the tower footprints and a museum beneath ground zero, sobering and beautifully done; book the museum ahead and allow a quiet couple of hours.

venues.name: Statue of Liberty & Ellis Island
venues.note: The harbour crossing and the immigration halls are the real experience, book crown or pedestal access weeks ahead through your advisor, as they sell out; families can trace ancestors in the Ellis Island records.

venues.name: Empire State Building
venues.note: The 86th-floor open-air deck still delivers the classic New York view; the redone second-floor museum is genuinely good. Go at dusk to catch daylight and the lit city in one visit.

venues.name: Top of the Rock, Rockefeller Center
venues.note: The best skyline view precisely because it looks back at the Empire State and up Central Park, three open decks, no glass in your photos. The new 'Beam' rooftop experience is a fun add-on.

venues.name: Summit One Vanderbilt
venues.area: Midtown East / next to Grand Central
venues.note: The most theatrical observation deck, mirrored rooms, glass-floor ledges over Madison Avenue and glass 'Ascent' lifts on the building's flank; part art installation, part view. Book a timed slot.

venues.name: Edge at Hudson Yards
venues.note: The Western Hemisphere's highest outdoor sky deck, with an angled glass floor and a lean-out corner over the West Side; adrenaline-seekers can add the 'City Climb' harnessed ascent up the building's exterior.

venues.name: One World Observatory
venues.note: Top of the tallest tower in the Western Hemisphere, a fast lift with a time-lapse of the city's rise, then harbour-to-Manhattan views. Best paired with the 9/11 Memorial below.

venues.name: The Staten Island Ferry
venues.note: The best free thing in New York, a 25-minute ride past the Statue of Liberty and the downtown skyline, no ticket, no queue. Ride out, turn around, ride back; go at golden hour.

venues.name: Central Park
venues.note: The 843-acre green heart of the city, the Bethesda Terrace, the Ramble, the Bow Bridge and the Reservoir loop; hire bikes or a rowboat, or take the kids to the zoo. A different world every season.

venues.name: The High Line
venues.note: A disused elevated freight line turned wild-planted walkway above the West Side, threading past galleries and river views; walk it end to end and step off into Chelsea's art scene or Hudson Yards.

venues.name: Little Island
venues.note: A pocket park floating over the Hudson on concrete 'tulips' by Heatherwick, undulating lawns, hidden overlooks and a small amphitheatre with summer performances. Free, and a lovely 20 minutes off the High Line.

venues.name: Brooklyn Bridge
venues.note: Walk the elevated wooden promenade from Manhattan into Brooklyn for the definitive skyline view; go early morning to have the cathedral-like stone arches nearly to yourself, then descend into DUMBO.

venues.name: Brooklyn Bridge Park & DUMBO
venues.note: Cobbled streets under the bridge, the Instagram-famous Washington Street view of the Manhattan Bridge, Jane's Carousel and a green waterfront that faces the whole downtown skyline. End the bridge walk here.

venues.name: Washington Square Park & Greenwich Village
venues.note: The marble arch, the fountain, the chess players and street musicians, the bohemian soul of the city, ringed by NYU and low townhouse streets perfect for aimless wandering.

venues.name: The West Village
venues.note: Crooked, tree-lined streets of red-brick townhouses, tiny bookshops and cafés, the prettiest walk in Manhattan and the loveliest for an unhurried morning. Bleecker and Perry streets are the postcard.

venues.name: SoHo
venues.note: The world's densest run of cast-iron architecture, now a cobblestoned luxury shopping quarter, flagship boutiques below, ornate 19th-century facades above. Look up as much as into the windows.
credentials: SoHo-Cast Iron Historic District, National Historic Landmark

venues.name: Chinatown & Little Italy
venues.note: One of the largest Chinese communities in the West, dim sum, tea shops and produce markets flowing into the last blocks of Little Italy on Mulberry Street; a sensory wander best done hungry.

venues.name: The Lower East Side
venues.note: The old immigrant tenement district turned gallery-and-cocktail neighbourhood; the Tenement Museum tells the story through restored apartments, then the streets deliver vintage shops and the New Museum.

venues.name: Harlem
venues.note: The capital of Black American culture, a Sunday gospel service, the Apollo Theater, soul food on Lenox Avenue and the Studio Museum; take a guided walk to read the history in the brownstones.

venues.name: Williamsburg
venues.note: Brooklyn's design-and-nightlife capital, independent boutiques, rooftop bars and the best Manhattan-skyline sunset in the city from the East River waterfront. Take the ferry over for the arrival.

venues.name: The Apollo Theater
venues.note: The stage where Ella Fitzgerald, James Brown and Aretha were made, catch the legendary Amateur Night or a show, or take the daytime tour of a true American music landmark.

venues.name: Broadway & the Theater District
venues.note: The world's benchmark for musical theatre, book a marquee show months ahead through your advisor; family groups can't go wrong with The Lion King or Aladdin. Skip Times Square itself once you've seen it.

venues.name: Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts
venues.note: The Metropolitan Opera, the New York Philharmonic and City Ballet around a floodlit travertine plaza and fountain, dress up for a Met Opera night, one of the great evenings out in the city.

venues.name: Carnegie Hall
venues.note: The most storied concert hall in America, with acoustics musicians travel the world to play, a recital here is a bucket-list evening; a backstage tour reveals the history if you can't catch a show.

venues.name: Village Vanguard & the Village jazz clubs
venues.note: The basement room where Coltrane and Bill Evans recorded live albums, still the holy ground of jazz. Book the early set; pair it with Blue Note or Smalls nearby for a proper night of music.

venues.name: Grand Central Terminal
venues.note: Not a station so much as a Beaux-Arts cathedral, the celestial-ceiling main concourse, the Whispering Gallery and an oyster bar in the vaults below. Free, always open, and quietly astonishing.

venues.name: The New York Public Library (Stephen A. Schwarzman Building)
venues.note: The marble-lion library whose Rose Reading Room, a football-field of chandeliers and painted clouds, is open to anyone who walks in; catch a free treasures exhibition and step next door into Bryant Park.

venues.name: Rockefeller Center
venues.note: An Art Deco city-within-a-city, the golden Prometheus and the sunken plaza (ice-skating in winter, the giant tree in December), Radio City next door and Top of the Rock above. The heart of Midtown.

venues.name: St. Patrick's Cathedral
venues.note: The great white Gothic-Revival cathedral facing Rockefeller Center, step in from the Fifth Avenue bustle for the soaring nave and rose window; a five-minute pause that resets the whole day.

venues.name: The Oculus & World Trade Center
venues.note: Calatrava's soaring white-ribbed transit hall, like a bird or a whale's skeleton in marble, now a luxury shopping concourse; the most dramatic piece of new architecture downtown, and free to walk through.

venues.name: Chelsea gallery district
venues.note: The world's densest concentration of contemporary art galleries, Gagosian, David Zwirner, Hauser & Wirth and dozens more, all free to enter. Spend a Saturday afternoon drifting between shows off the High Line.

venues.name: Chelsea Market
venues.note: A former Nabisco biscuit factory turned covered food hall, lobster, tacos, artisan pastry and design shops in brick-and-pipe arcades; graze your way through, then step straight onto the High Line above.

venues.name: Grand Central Market & Great Northern Food Hall
venues.note: Within and beside the terminal, a European-style market of cheese, seafood and fresh bread, and Nordic food stalls under the arches. A civilised graze while you admire the building.

venues.name: Smorgasburg
venues.note: America's largest open-air food market, a hundred-odd vendors of everything from ramen burgers to mango sticky rice, with the Manhattan skyline behind. Weekends only, and a great way to eat your way through Brooklyn.

venues.name: Fifth Avenue & Madison Avenue shopping
venues.note: The full spectrum of luxury, the marquee flagships and Bergdorf Goodman on Fifth, the quieter European maisons and galleries up Madison. Your advisor can arrange private appointments and after-hours access.

venues.name: SoHo boutiques
venues.note: The most stylish shopping in the city, flagship fashion, concept stores and independent design along cast-iron blocks; less crowded and more curated than Fifth Avenue, and made for wandering on foot.

venues.name: A Central Park bike or pedicab ride
venues.note: The loveliest way to see the whole park in an hour, hire bikes at Columbus Circle, or take a guided pedicab to the film locations and hidden corners. Gentler and more private than the carriage horses.

venues.name: A Hudson River sunset sail
venues.note: Board a classic schooner or private yacht for a sail past the Statue of Liberty as the skyline lights up, the single most romantic hour in New York, and easily chartered privately through your advisor.

venues.name: A Manhattan helicopter tour
venues.note: Fifteen minutes over the harbour, the Statue of Liberty and the length of the skyline, the view that puts the whole city in one frame; ask your advisor about doors-off or private charters.

venues.name: The Roosevelt Island Tramway
venues.note: A commuter aerial cable-car, on a subway swipe, that glides over the East River beside the Queensboro Bridge for a five-minute skyline ride; a quiet thrill most visitors never find.

venues.name: Prospect Park & the Brooklyn Botanic Garden
venues.note: The same designers' 'better' park than Central Park, meadows, a lake and a ravine with fewer crowds, beside a botanic garden famed for its spring cherry blossom and Japanese pond. A perfect Brooklyn morning.

venues.name: Green-Wood Cemetery
venues.note: A 478-acre Victorian garden cemetery of rolling hills, glacial ponds and Gothic gates, resting place of Basquiat and Bernstein, with the best hidden harbour view in Brooklyn. Wildly atmospheric and almost empty.

venues.name: The Cathedral of St. John the Divine
venues.note: The largest Gothic cathedral in the world, still famously unfinished, a vast, cool, half-built nave with a peacock in the close. Deeply atmospheric, and paired well with a Columbia University stroll.

venues.name: The Tenement Museum
venues.note: Restored immigrant apartments in a preserved 1863 tenement, told through the real families who lived there, the most moving history lesson in the city, and resonant for anyone whose own family emigrated. Book a tour ahead.

venues.name: Storm King Art Center
venues.note: A 500-acre open-air sculpture park where monumental Calders, Serras and Goldsworthys sit in rolling meadows and woods, a full day of art and landscape; hire bikes on arrival. A superb warm-weather day trip.

venues.name: The Hamptons
venues.note: The summer-weekend playground of Manhattan's elite, ocean beaches, hedge-lined estates, farm stands and East Hampton village; best mid-week to avoid the crowds. Your advisor can arrange a house or a beach club.

venues.name: Bemelmans Bar
venues.note: The most beautiful bar in New York, Ludwig Bemelmans' murals, a grand piano, a perfect martini.
credentials: A globally historic cocktail bar, inside The Carlyle

venues.name: The Dead Rabbit
venues.note: A former World's Best Bar reviving the lost art of the New York-Irish tavern.

venues.name: Katana Kitten
venues.note: A Japanese-American izakaya bar that has ranked among the world's best for years.
credentials: Former World's Best Bar in America

venues.name: Overstory
venues.note: Cocktails on the 64th floor with a 360-degree sweep of the harbour and the skyline.

venues.name: Double Chicken Please
venues.note: An inventive back-room bar that was recently ranked the best in North America.
credentials: World's 50 Best Bars, former No. 1 in North America

venues.name: The King Cole Bar
venues.note: The birthplace of the Bloody Mary, beneath Maxfield Parrish's mural, old-money New York.
credentials: A globally historic cocktail bar, inside The St. Regis

venues.name: Attaboy
venues.note: A no-menu speakeasy where you name a spirit and a mood, bespoke drinks, no fuss.

venues.name: The Aviary NYC
venues.note: A theatrical cocktail laboratory high in the Mandarin Oriental, drinks as edible art.
credentials: A bar of international standing, from the Alinea Group

venues.name: Employees Only
venues.note: A speakeasy that helped start the modern cocktail revival, buzzy well past midnight.

venues.name: The Rooftop at Pier 17
venues.note: Drinks and skyline views by the Brooklyn Bridge, the river breeze on a summer night.
credentials: A landmark rooftop venue at the Seaport
